description: About Us & Our Challenge: Hello Space Explorers! We are a passionate duo—a Software Developer and a UI/UX Designer—taking on Challenge 12. Planet X and SPHEREx in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our goal is to build an interactive astronomical tool that explores infrared data and helps study distant celestial objects.
summary:
**SPHEREx Explorer** is a web-based astronomical exploration tool designed to help users investigate how celestial objects and their surrounding fields change across observations. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, the application provides five predefined challenge targets and a custom coordinate exploration workflow.

Users can explore authentic SPHEREx Level 2 FITS observations through an interactive viewer featuring side-by-side image comparison, automatic blinking between observations, synchronized zoom, image stretching, brightness controls, and observation metadata. The application also includes a pilot spatial index for locating available observations by sky coordinates.

By making complex astronomical data easier to explore and compare, SPHEREx Explorer aims to help users identify potential changes in celestial objects over time and make scientific observations more accessible. Its modular architecture provides a foundation for expanding archive coverage, spectral analysis, and automated object discovery.
details:
Project Details — SPHEREx Explorer

SPHEREx Explorer is an interactive web application developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. It aims to make astronomical observations easier to explore, visualize, and compare over time.

The application provides five predefined challenge targets and a custom coordinate exploration interface where users can enter Right Ascension (RA), Declination (Dec), and Field of View (FOV) to investigate available observation coverage.

Its authentic-data demonstration uses real SPHEREx Level 2 FITS observations obtained through NASA/IPAC IRSA. A custom JavaScript FITS parser reads the Multi-Extension FITS structure, extracts scientific image arrays, and preserves observation metadata, quality flags, and uncertainty information.

The Sky Viewer provides side-by-side observation comparison and automatic blinking between images, with synchronized zoom, image stretching, brightness controls, and inversion. A dedicated information panel displays observation identifiers, timestamps, detector bands, coordinates, and relevant scientific metadata.

The project uses React, Vite, JavaScript, CSS, HTML5 Canvas, and browser-based FITS processing. Its design focuses on combining scientific data accessibility with an interactive exploration experience inspired by astronomical time-domain tools.

SPHEREx Explorer aims to help students, astronomy enthusiasts, and researchers visually investigate changes across observations and identify potential candidates for further scientific analysis. Its modular architecture provides a foundation for future expansion into broader archive coverage, spectral exploration, source detection, and motion analysis.

Data transparency: The Custom Archive demonstration includes authentic SPHEREx FITS observations from a limited pilot field. Preset demonstration sequences are clearly identified as synthetic where authentic observation coverage has not been established. The application does not present simulated observations as real scientific measurements.
